texts: doha on a thief with sweet words, hovering like a fly around victims
A smooth-talking man sold my mother a worthless policy; he buzzed around her like a fly, was extremely polite, and next day vanished like a thief.
thief, fly, false smile
The thief wears a smile as sweet as a friend's greeting, and the fly of false friendliness follows the scent of trust.
Please write a doha about how a thief who speaks sweetly is far more dangerous than one who breaks in at night, because a fly of false friendliness hovers around until he finds your weakness.
doha on people with two faces, nice to ur face and nasty behind
Could you write a doha about the person who wears one face for the crowd and another in private, smiling and flattering while he plans harm, so that nobody can ever really trust a word he says?
One face for the crowd, another for the hour of plotting; the double-faced man deceives even himself.
My business partner praised me at the meeting and then quietly took my clients the next week, and I am still stunned.
two-faced, can't trust

Compose a doha for the cheat who wears a mask of devotion, speaks of fire and holy vows, and rides in a palanquin while he robs the villagers who trusted him, showing that the cunning are always found out.
The preacher who arrived in a palanquin, speaking fiery words about charity, left our village with all its donations and not a word of thanks.
He rode in a palanquin and spoke words of fire, yet the cheat's pockets were full of the poor man's trust.
palanquin, fire, cheating preacher
doha on a fake holy man in a doli with fiery speeches who cheated everyone
honeyed words, bitter aim
A man at the bus stand was so kind to my grandfather, offered him tea, and walked off with his wallet.
Please write a doha about how people who speak the sweetest words to your face are often the ones with the worst intentions, and how we must look at their deeds and not just their talk.
Sweet is the voice of the deceiver, yet bitter is the purpose it hides.
doha for ppl who are super nice but turn out to be frauds
doha on cheating someone, it always comes back
The fraud thrives for a season; but trust, once betrayed, never returns to the betrayer's hands.
I'd like a doha about how the person who cheats another gains a small profit now but loses a name, friendships and peace of mind for life, so that in the end he is the poorest of all.
fraud ruins the fraud
My cousin cheated his friend on a land deal and now no family in our town will let him sit at their table.
Can you write me a doha about how the cheat who adds salt to the true weight of his goods fools the poor buyer, but cannot fool his own conscience, which keeps count of every falsehood until the end?
The vendor mixed salt in the spice he sold me and swore it was pure, and I trusted his smiling face.
doha on someone who cheats with salt in the goods
The cheat sprinkles salt in the pure grain, but the account of his lies is kept elsewhere.
salt, cheating trader
swan, fire, false saint
The swan wears white and the fire hides in the ember; deceit too puts on a spotless outer robe.
A man dressed in spotless white like a swan came to our colony, and by the time the fire from his tall promises died down, our savings were gone.
doha on a fake swan with fire inside, a cheat dressed pure
Write a doha about the man in snow-white garments who looks like a gentle swan but whose fire of greed burns the trusting, showing that trickery can wear the most innocent colours.
A pearl of speech on the lip, a plot in the mind; the deceiver dazzles with words but starves the trusting.
Could you write a doha about the pearl-like words of a flatterer that dazzle the ear but hide plans to take advantage, so that the wise listener tests every sweet phrase before accepting it?
pearl words, false heart
My new neighbour kept showering us with pearl-like compliments until she had borrowed all our savings, and now she does not answer the phone.
doha on flattery as a pearl that hides a lie
He smiled at me all through the party and told everyone I was his best friend, but I later found he had applied for my job behind my back.
doha on friends who stab u in the back
Compose a doha about the false friend who laughs with you at the feast and plots to ruin you, showing that one must judge a person by his actions in hard times and not his words in good times.
His smile is a cover and his words are soft; behind both the traitor lays his plan.
false friend, hidden plan
The man who sold us the plot of land swore on his mother, but all we found was a bundle of ash and paperwork that meant nothing.
doha on fraud that turns into ash in ur hands
Compose a doha showing that the profit of deceit turns to ash in the hands of the cheat, no matter how clever the scheme, because falsehood has no roots and cannot hold anything for long.
The wealth of fraud turns to ash in the hand; only honest gain remains.
ash, fraud's reward
At the cremation ground the cheat finds his fine speech meaningless, for no lie can bribe the final hour.
My uncle cheated dozens of people in his lifetime, and at the cremation ground I could see no one who truly mourned him.
cremation ground, liar's end
Write a doha showing that the cheat who builds his life on lies finds only an empty cremation ground at the end, where nobody weeps for him because he never gave anyone a reason to trust him.
doha on frauds ending up alone at the cremation ground

Write a doha about the person who speaks sweet and smiling words while secretly nursing harmful intentions, and how such pretence may fool people for a short while but is always revealed by the quiet test of time.
doha on fake niceness and hidden bad intent
Our landlord was so warm when we signed the lease, and the minute we moved in he started inventing charges to squeeze more money from us.
Behind the courteous greeting hides a cold purpose; let me learn to read the face behind the face.
smiling deceiver
hey doha on liars who cheat the innocent
I want a doha saying that trickery may win a battle but lose the war, because whoever deceives others must keep inventing more lies to cover the first, and soon he is trapped by his own falsehoods.
cheating never pays
My classmate copied my work and then told the teacher I copied his, and I stood there too shocked to even speak.
One lie needs seven more to stand; the cheat builds on weakness and calls it strength.
doha on soft cotton words hiding a nasty plan
The cotton trader spoke so gently while weighing my bale, yet he somehow got away with a fifth of what I brought.

Please write a doha about the person who speaks soft as cotton and promises everything, but whose real purpose is to take advantage of your trust, so that the careful ones learn to weigh actions rather than words.
Soft as cotton are his promises, yet each one hides a hook for the unwary.
cotton words, cheating
The glass that imitates a diamond may fool the eye, but never the jeweller's test; so the false are found.
My cousin bought a so-called diamond ring on a street corner for a bargain, only to find a piece of glass, and the seller was gone.
fake diamond, fraud
doha on fake diamonds and scammers

Could you write a doha about a cheat who sells glass pretending it is a diamond, showing that honest worth lasts while false shine fades, and the deceiver's fortune disappears when the buyer finally sees the truth?

Compose a doha about how a snake that charms with a gentle swaying motion is far more dangerous than one that hisses openly, just as the flatterer with a pleasant manner is to be feared more than the honest enemy.
doha on smiling people like snakes, can't trust them
snake, false friendliness
My supervisor greets everyone warmly while quietly reporting each of us for small slips; he moves like a snake in the grass.
The snake that bows and sways has fang beneath its grace; beware the smiling visitor.
My boss walks into the meeting with a roar like a lion, then turns into a lamb when the director is around, and cheats all of us when it suits him.
Compose a doha about a man who is a lion to those below him and a mouse to those above, showing the fraud of a person who changes faces to suit his advantage and deserves no trust from anyone.
A lion to the weak, a lamb to the strong; the double-faced man has no true face.
doha on bosses who act like lions to us but lick up to their seniors
lion, false front
trust no flatterer
My co-worker praised every idea I had and then presented them to the manager as her own.
Praise sung too sweetly is suspect; look for the motive behind the flattering song.
Write a doha showing that a person who cheats others by pretending to be a friend carries guilt in his own mind and can never rest, whether in company or alone, until he confesses and makes good.
doha about backstabbers who pretend to be friends
The rose is beautiful and the thorn beneath is hidden; the cheat's smile is the same.
My new boyfriend was so charming at the start, but a thorn of lies kept appearing, and after six months I found out he had been seeing someone else.
thorn, hidden harm
Compose a doha about how a pleasing face and gracious words often conceal a thorn, so that we must be careful before we trust a stranger, and learn to read behaviour rather than appearance.
doha on charming ppl who turn out to be thorns

Write a doha about the bitter gourd that looks like any other vegetable but turns the whole meal bitter once it is in the mouth, just as a deceitful person looks pleasant but sours every relationship he enters.
The bitter gourd wears the green of health and carries the taste of poison; so does the liar's friendship.
bitter gourd, false friend
doha on bitter gourd = fake friend
My brother-in-law looks decent enough but, like a bitter gourd, he turns every family meeting sour with his lies and schemes.
After he borrowed money pretending to have a sick child, we found out he gambled it all away on the same day.
Pity pretended, need counterfeited; the cheat's tears flow where truth has long since dried.
I'd like a doha about the man who pretends to be sick, poor or desperate to win sympathy and money from kind people, and about how his false tears cost the real needy their chance of help.
fake tears
doha on scammers who fake sob stories
doha on a thief who pretends to be honest
A man came to our colony claiming to be a retired officer, charmed everyone, and then one night our thief-like guest was gone with several valuables.
Compose a doha about the thief who lives among honest people in a good man's clothing, and about how the day his mask slips, the trust he took is lost forever and cannot be won back by apology.
The thief in the garb of the honest has the sweetest face; only time unmasks him.
thief, honest mask
The yogi in saffron near the ocean promised to double our money through prayers; we paid him gladly, and then he vanished like a wave.
yogi, ocean, fraud
doha on a fake yogi cheating ppl by the ocean
Write a doha about a fake yogi who sits beside the ocean pretending to meditate while he reads the pockets of the pilgrims who come to him, and how real holiness never asks for money in return.
The ocean is vast, but the fake yogi's greed is wider; his holy robes hide a hungry hand.
cheat, be careful

Please write a doha explaining that the swindler's greatest skill is to make the victim believe he is being helped, so that honest people must always check the claims of strangers before handing over their trust or their savings.
doha on scammers who act like helpers
Someone called me from the bank, knew my name and some details, and almost got my pin number before I hung up.
The deceiver speaks of help while his hand reaches for your savings; guard your trust carefully.
fraud, fake smile
Beware the honeyed greeting, for the cheat's welcome is the first step in the plan to ruin you.

Compose a doha showing that those who say one thing and do another, praising principles in public and breaking them in private, carry a divided character that eventually brings them shame and loss of every honest friend.
doha on ppl who say one thing and do another
My uncle lectured us all on honesty for years and then we found out he had been cooking the accounts at work.
My neighbour came with a needle to mend my curtain, and while smiling like a snake, she made copies of my keys.
needle, snake, trickery
The needle seems gentle; the snake seems harmless; both are cruel to the one who trusts.
doha with needle and snake, helpful liars
Could you write a doha that says a person who pretends to help like a needle mending cloth while moving like a snake to harm you is the most dangerous of all, because he is trusted?
Beneath the pleasant word the cheat keeps his plan, and he who trusts too quickly pays too much.
After the agent assured me the car had never been in an accident, I found out it had been hit three times and repainted.
false promise
Write a doha showing that those who cheat do so because they lack the courage to earn honestly, and that the person who lives with deception will always be nervous about being found out in the end.
doha on liars who sell fake things
doha on cheating in exams, felt so guilty
I copied my friend's answers in the exam and got higher marks than her; I still feel awful every time she congratulates me.
cheating, guilty conscience

Please write a doha explaining that a victory won by cheating is a defeat in disguise, because the cheat knows what he has done even if nobody else does, and carries that knowledge like a hidden weight forever.
Success gained by cheating is borrowed; the borrower never feels it is his own.
doha on a washerman who cheats ppl and a palace that is full of liars

Compose a doha about a washerman who returns the wrong garments and denies it, and about the palace where courtiers smile at the king while plotting against him, showing that cheating exists at every level of society.
palace, washerman, cheating
The washerman and the courtier both cheat; one in a lane, the other in a palace, and both shame their name.
The washerman mixed up our garments and swore he hadn't, while at the palace function the minister's smile hid some serious scheming.
Write a doha saying that the one who sets a trap for others is first to fall into it, so a clever man is not one who tricks others but one honest enough to avoid trickery.
traps catch trappers
He who plots another's ruin plans his own; the schemer is the architect of his fall.
doha on karma for people who play tricks
My co-worker tried to get me fired by spreading false stories, and he is the one who got dismissed last month.
false charm
doha on ppl who act kind just to use others
She was my best friend until she got the promotion, and then she did not return a single call, and I realised she'd been using me.
Friendship feigned for gain is no friendship; the self-serving smile hides a list of favours owed.

Please write a doha about the people who make friends only when they need something, flatter you in difficult days, and disappear when your fortune changes, showing that false friendship is simply a business of the heart.
Could you write a doha for the dishonest dealer who shortchanges customers a little every day and believes nobody notices, though in the end all those small thefts are repaid in full with interest?
The dealer in our area shortchanged us a little every month for years, and the day we discovered it, nobody would ever buy from him again.
doha on small daily cheating adds up
A little each day he takes from the trusting; but the account of years comes due in a single hour.
petty cheating
Smiling lips and scheming mind: the pair that has ruined more lives than open enemies ever could.

Compose a doha about the difference between an honest enemy and a hidden one, because the honest foe warns you of his intentions while the false friend comes smiling and strikes when you are least expecting.
doha on smiling backstabbers vs open enemies
hidden enemy, smiling face
I would rather face my rival at work than my so-called friend, who is sweet in public and leaks my mistakes to the boss.
doha on a cuckoo that lays eggs in other nests, a cheat
The cuckoo's song is sweet, but she leaves her young in a stranger's care; beware of music that hides a cheat.
Can you write a doha about the cuckoo who sings sweetly yet leaves her eggs in another bird's nest for them to raise, showing that a pleasing voice can hide a selfish and deceitful nature?
My sister has a lovely cuckoo-like voice, and she charms everyone, but she keeps leaving her responsibilities to other people.
cuckoo, sweet but selfish
doha on people who promise a lot but never deliver
Write a doha showing that the person who promises everything and delivers nothing is more harmful than an honest refusal, because he gives hope and then steals it, leaving the trusting one worse off.
Promises given in plenty, yet nothing follows; the faithless fill the air with sweetness and leave the soul empty.
empty promises
The contractor kept promising our roof would be ready next week for six months, taking more money each time, and nothing ever happened.
palanquin, false groom
The groom's family arrived with a grand palanquin and promises of a rich life, and only after the wedding did we learn it was all a pretence to take my sister's dowry.
Please write a doha about the family that arrives for the wedding with a palanquin full of show and promises but hides their greed, showing that pomp is often the cheat's finest costume.
doha on fake rich ppl at weddings in a palanquin, they cheat the bride's family
The palanquin is bright and the promises are brighter; but the bride finds the groom's family empty.
He made me believe that we were going to be partners, and I learnt only later that he never had the slightest intention of keeping his word.
His word was soft, his meaning hard; the trusting soul is the cheat's richest gain.

Please write a doha explaining that people who deceive in business never prosper for long, because the world is small and the news of one betrayal travels farther and faster than a hundred honest deals.
false partner
doha on business partner who cheated me
He builds his fortune on sand and draws his water from a well of lies, and the first rain exposes it all.
doha on a well and sand, a cheating moneyman who builds on sand
Compose a doha showing that wealth built on deceit is like a well dug in the sand, which seems promising at first but collapses at the first rain and leaves nothing for the cheat or his victims.
Our village contractor built a well on sandy ground to save money and cheated the whole panchayat, and the first rains swallowed it.
well, sand, fraud
The cloud of promises he spread over our village brought no rain, and by the time the farmers realised they were being cheated, the leader had gone.
A cloud that thunders but sheds no rain is the cheat's word, loud and empty.
cloud, false promises

Compose a doha showing that the false leader is like a cloud that promises rain and thunders loudly, but passes over without giving a single drop, leaving the farmers' fields dry and their hopes broken.
doha on politicians promising like clouds but giving no rain
doha on a fish caught by a fake bait, deceit
The fish takes the bait for food, not seeing the hook; so the trusting soul is caught by the cheat's kindness.
fish, bait, trickery
My aunt fell for an online scheme that promised high returns, like a fish swallowing bait, and lost all her savings.
Write a doha showing that as the fisherman tempts the fish with bait that hides a hook, a cheat tempts the simple with promises that conceal his purpose, and only the careful avoid the trap.
fish, bait, trap
They offered my father a free holiday in exchange for his bank details, and I told him the fish never sees the hook until it is too late.
The fish loves the bait and forgets the hook; the greedy are caught by the cheat's open hand.
Write a doha about how greedy people are caught like a fish by the bait of the cheat's promises, because they want quick profits and ignore the warning signs that careful people notice at once.
doha with a fish: greed makes u fall for scams

Compose a doha about people who show devotion with loud prayers and long vows while cheating their neighbours in business, showing that false piety is the worst form of dishonesty and cannot hide from the Almighty.
doha on religious ppl who cheat in daily life
cheating pious frauds
The man who leads prayers in our colony is the same one who sells the grain with a false measure; everyone knows but nobody dares to say.
His lips are wet with holy names, his hands are quick with false measures; the Lord sees both.

Write a doha about the temple trustee who collects donations in the name of God and uses them for his own luxury, showing that deceit in holy places is the most shameful and invites the heaviest reckoning.
temple, donation fraud
The trustee of our temple built a new car garage from the offerings, and the poor devotees who gave their last coins had no idea.
He took in the name of God, and spent in the name of self; the temple weeps for such guardians.
doha on a fraud who steals donations from the temple
doha on a pearl dealer who cheats with fake pearls
pearl, cheating dealer
A false pearl glitters in the dealer's palm; only a sharp eye separates the true from the fabricated.
I bought a pearl necklace on holiday for a high price and later learnt it was a cheap imitation.
Please write a doha about the dealer who sells false pearls at the price of true ones, with a sweet smile and a warm handshake, and how one false deal ruins a lifetime's reputation.

Write a doha about how a person who pretends to be poor to receive help, while hiding wealth, steals not only money but the kindness that the truly poor need, and eventually dries up the world's compassion.
doha on fake poverty to get sympathy
I gave money every week to a woman who said she had no food, and then I saw her get into a car and drive away.
pretending to be poor
The cheat who borrows poverty steals from the truly poor, and the kindness of the world grows cold.
Could you write a doha comparing the rainbird that sings of pure rain with a cheat who calls fake metal gold and promises a shower of wealth, showing how false hopes leave the thirsty with nothing?
doha on rainbird and fake gold, scam promises
A scheme promised to turn our small savings into gold within a season, like a rainbird promised rain, and the organisers vanished before the first month ended.
rainbird, gold, scam
The rainbird cries for rain, and the cheat cries gold; the thirsty believe both and are left dry.
cunning, honest heart wins
doha on how honesty beats trickery in the long run
My brother always took shortcuts and fooled people, while I stayed honest and poor, but today his customers are gone and mine stay on.
Honesty is slow yet arrives; trickery is quick and ends in ruin.

Please write a doha about how the trickster seems to win in the short run, but honesty and fairness prove far stronger over a lifetime, because people always return to those whom they can trust without doubt.
lies have short life

Write a doha saying that falsehood and cheating look strong for a day but cannot survive the truth, so a person who builds his future on deception builds on something that will not stand the first test.
My friend lied on his resume to get a job, and in the first month it all came apart in front of everyone.
Falsehood is quick to rise and quick to fall; only the true endures.
doha on lies not lasting long
pearl, fake pearl
My father, an honest jeweller, was cheated by a smooth stranger who gave him a counterfeit pearl in return for a real one.
Compose a doha about how a counterfeit pearl may look as radiant as the true one, but a person who deals in fakes loses the trust that no real pearl can ever buy back.
doha on someone swapping a real pearl for a fake
Counterfeit pearls pass from hand to hand, but the honest eye of time knows the true from the false.
doha on separating pearls from fakes with a winnowing fan
The winnowing fan blows off the chaff of lies; what remains is the honest pearl.

Write a doha showing that the winnowing fan of discernment separates the false from the true, as it does chaff from grain, and the pearl of honest dealing is what remains for the wise after the cheating is blown away.
After months of getting cheated by the sweet-talking sellers, I learnt to winnow out the honest ones like pearls from chaff.
winnowing fan, pearl, cheat
